Alaska.Ai — Anchorage Desk Draft

2026-09-11 · branch claude/linkedin-desk-2026-09-11

Copy this for LinkedIn

Jared Goecker, Eagle River’s Anchorage Assembly member, voted Sept. 1 in the 8-4 majority that funded APD’s Real-Time Crime Center expansion. Just under $600,000 moved before the rules for the system did.

The contract is with Thundercat, not to exceed $598,998.10 per Alaska’s News Source, paid from federal asset forfeitures according to the memorandum ADN reported. It buys audio-visual equipment and desks to move a center that already exists out of what Chief Sean Case described as a small concrete box at the Elmore Road building.

The hub can reach roughly 750 cameras, including more than 250 traffic cameras, body cameras, drones and volunteered private security feeds, per Alaska Public Media.

Goecker took issue with the Assembly’s August postponement, citing a state Department of Public Safety report showing Anchorage property crime up 20% last year. On the record he said “Delaying resources for law enforcement while crime is surging is completely backwards and unacceptable.” He chose fund now, with seven colleagues, over the four (McCormick, Volland, Scout, Martinez) who wanted the surveillance-and-privacy ordinance adopted first.

That’s a legitimate governing position rather than a talking point. Kameron Perez-Verdia, also in support, put the sunk-cost point plainly. Holding back audio-visual equipment for a center that’s already functioning and already processing information didn’t make sense to him. The forfeiture funding lowers the fiscal stakes of yes, and a month’s delay against that crime report is a real cost the privacy side has to answer for.

The evidence-backed risk is sequencing, and Goecker owns it. The majority authorized a platform that can reach 750 cameras two weeks before the Assembly returns to the ordinance that would require its own approval for any AI deployment on that platform, two-week deletion of footage not tied to active investigations, and warrants before sharing data with federal agencies. Case told the Assembly in August that “Code is not going to keep up with technology.” Capability is going in ahead of its rules, on a system whose own chief expects the code to lag.

His next vote is on that ordinance, sponsored by McCormick, Volland and Scout, which Volland says the sponsors plan to bring back before the Assembly on Sept. 15 after fine tuning with the mayor’s administration. Watch whether the same eight-member majority that funded the hardware now constrains the AI that will run on it, waters the provisions down, or defers the guardrails again. Goecker’s own reasoning cuts both ways. If delay is unacceptable for law-enforcement resources, the same clock is running on the rulebook.

Was funding the Thundercat buildout two weeks ahead of the ordinance the right sequence, or should the eight have tied the money to the rules?

#AlaskaAI #AIPolicy #ProcurementReform

Editor note:
TARGET. Jared Goecker, Anchorage Assembly member representing Eagle River. Decision dated 1 Sep 2026 (his vote in the 8-4 majority funding the Thundercat expansion of APD's Real-Time Crime Center), inside the 60-day window. No window broadening. All seven gate points plus the conflict screen passed. Validator confidence MEDIUM, for the reason below.

SOURCING CAVEAT (read this one). muni.org returned HTTP 403 and anchorageak.legistar.com would not resolve through the proxy, so the 8-4 roll call, the memorandum number and Goecker's seat are journalist-reported (Alaska Public Media 3 Sep, Alaska's News Source 1 Sep, ADN 31 Aug, Alaska Public Media 21 Aug), not fetched from a signed Legistar record. Goecker's status as a voting Eagle River member and his one verbatim quote ARE confirmed on the fetched Alaska Public Media primary. The orchestrator re-fetched every source and scrubbed two scout-supplied figures that appeared on no fetched page ("$11.8M previously approved system" and memorandum "AM 524-2026"); neither is in the post. The ordinance number AO 2026-108 was also kept out of the body (carried only from the 28 Aug dossier and a muni.org document title). The 15 Sep date is phrased as the ordinance coming back before the Assembly, as the source says, not as a public hearing.

SELECTION NOTE. Daniel Volland (NO vote plus co-sponsorship) passed the gate with higher confidence but was dropped on a new-angle tiebreaker: he would have been the fourth privacy-side profile of this thread (Case 7 Aug, McCormick 14 Aug, Scout 28 Aug). Goecker is the first approve-side profile. This is still the fourth consecutive Desk post on the RTCC thread; consider rotating off it next cycle unless the 15 Sep ordinance vote produces a genuinely new owner. Other drops: Wolfson / DeepGreen (subject-owned filing predates the window; Massachusetts-based), Reed / Northrim-Narmi and Siemers / UAA LIFT Center (single-org sourcing), Dotson / UAA symposium (convening, not a consequential binary). Founders, operators and research slices were thin; municipal was rich. No scout stalls.

EDIT LOOP. Writer v1 overshot both caps (3,064 chars, 478 words). Orchestrator applied mechanical trims (v2, 2,988 / 464). Editor returned REVISE on one item only, a missing HEADLINE block in the body file, which the writer had delivered separately (it feeds the artwork, not the post), so it was treated as satisfied. The editor's optional cuts were applied (v3, 2,850 / 444): the redundant bio paragraph, the AO number, a paragraph split and one spelling consistency fix. Scorer: 9.21 / 10 against config/desk_rubric.yaml, no hard-fail, ship. Weakest criterion Readability (8): the scorer's suggested paragraph split was applied after scoring (a line break only, no wording change).

ARTWORK. Bespoke piece via the alaska-ai-artwork skill (style family wpa_scaffold, hue teal, composition diagonal_thrust; concept: the lit hub built, the handrail still a dashed drawing). Six eval iterations, final self-score 8.6 (floor 8.5), qa_check PASS, 1080x1080. Hosted at the commit-SHA-pinned raw.githubusercontent.com URL shown under the image.

PROCESS DEVIATIONS. (1) The scheduled prompt stored for this routine predates PR #106; it still points Phase 8 at the legacy alaska-ai-brief template and Phase 9 at base64 embedding. The repo's live prompts/desk_instructions.md designates the artwork skill as primary and requires the SHA-pinned hosted image URL, so this run followed the live repo version for Phases 8 to 10. Consider refreshing the stored routine prompt. (2) gh is not installed in the cloud VM; the draft PR was opened through the GitHub MCP connector instead. Carries the 8-4 vote, Goecker's verbatim quote and Eagle River identification, the 750-camera capacity, and the Sept. 15 return of the ordinance.

Confirms the Thundercat vendor, ~750 cameras incl. 250+ traffic cameras, and the ordinance's AI-approval, two-week deletion, LPR and federal-warrant provisions.
  • Municipality of Anchorage Assembly (NOT FETCHED, HTTP 403 via proxy) — — Assembly public-safety hub with the ordinance PDF and meeting records. Not reachable this run; roll call and memorandum number are therefore journalist-reported.
